summaryText:
In week four of the Planted series, called "Planted to Produce," Pastor Travis taught from Jesus' words about the vine and the branches in John 15. He reminded the church that God did not save us to remain spiritually stagnant. He called us to bear lasting fruit, and he said healthy roots produce healthy fruit. The service also honored mothers on Mother's Day, with a gentle acknowledgment that the day can be hard for some.

Pastor Travis shared three main thoughts. First, planted people produce fruit, not just feelings. Emotional highs and moments of hype come and go, but real fruit is shown in character. He walked through the fruit of the Spirit in Galatians 5:22-23 and encouraged believers to grow in love, joy, peace, patience, faithfulness, and self-control. He noted that fruit grows slowly, often underground and out of sight, so we are called to remain with God and not merely visit. He cautioned against wanting fruit without roots.

Second, planted people get pruned so they can produce more. Drawing on John 15:2 and Hebrews 12:6, he explained that pruning can feel like loss, yet it reflects a loving Father who refuses to leave His children immature. Sometimes God removes things that are good to make room for what is great. He invited listeners to become root inspectors of their own lives, asking whether bitterness, unforgiveness, pride, compromise, or unhealthy influences may be harming their spiritual roots. He encouraged praying Psalm 139:23, "Search me, God, and know my heart," and distinguished between the Holy Spirit's loving conviction and condemnation. He also pointed to Revelation 2 and the call to return to our first love.

Third, planted people do not just take in, they pour out. A fruit tree exists for the benefit of others. Pastor Travis contrasted immature believers who consume with mature believers who contribute, and he used the Dead Sea as an image of taking in without giving out. Citing John 7:38, he said a river flows while a swamp stagnates. He encouraged serving and sharing, noting that one planted life can bless a family, a workplace, and a generation.

The message closed with an invitation to surrender to Jesus for the first time and to be planted in God's Word, with many hands raised in response, followed by a prayer of salvation and a prayer of blessing for mothers. Online viewers were encouraged to connect through the Impact Church app, the connection card, and a QR code to share next steps or give.
mainPoints: Planted people produce lasting fruit of the Spirit, not just passing feelings, and real fruit grows slowly from deep roots as we remain in Christ.
Planted people get pruned so they can produce more: God lovingly removes even good things and exposes hidden roots so that we can grow healthier and more fruitful.
Planted people do not just take in, they pour out: mature believers contribute and serve so that rivers of living water flow to others.

versesMentioned.text: "I am the true vine, and my Father is the gardener. He cuts off every branch in me that bears no fruit, while every branch that does bear fruit he prunes so that it will be even more fruitful. You are already clean because of the word I have spoken to you. Remain in me, as I also remain in you. No branch can bear fruit by itself; it must remain in the vine. Neither can you bear fruit unless you remain in me. "I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit; apart from me you can do nothing. If you do not remain in me, you are like a branch that is thrown away and withers; such branches are picked up, thrown into the fire and burned. If you remain in me and my words remain in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you. This is to my Father's glory, that you bear much fruit, showing yourselves to be my disciples."
By their fruit you will recognize them. Do people pick grapes from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, forbearance, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. Against such things there is no law.
Because the Lord disciplines the one he loves, and he chastens everyone he accepts as his child.

"For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways," declares the Lord. "As the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways and my thoughts than your thoughts."

Yet I hold this against you: You have forsaken the love you had at first. Consider how far you have fallen! Repent and do the things you did at first. If you do not repent, I will come to you and remove your lampstand from its place.
Search me, God, and know my heart; test me and know my anxious thoughts.
Whoever believes in me, as Scripture has said, rivers of living water will flow from within them.

Monday.scripture: John 15:4 (NIV): "Remain in me, as I also remain in you. No branch can bear fruit by itself; it must remain in the vine."
Monday.focus: Remaining in Christ, not just visiting.
Monday.action: Set aside 10 minutes at the start of your day to read John 15:1-8 slowly and quietly. Write down one way you can stay connected to Jesus throughout the week.
Monday.prayer: Jesus, You are the vine and I am the branch. Help me to remain in You today and every day, and not just visit. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Galatians 5:22-23 (NIV): "But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, forbearance, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control."
Tuesday.focus: Character that shows lasting fruit, not passing feelings.
Tuesday.action: Read through the fruit of the Spirit and choose one you want to grow in this week. Practice it in one specific situation today, such as offering patience or kindness to someone.
Tuesday.prayer: Holy Spirit, grow Your fruit in my life. Help my character, and not just my feelings, reflect Jesus today. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: Psalm 139:23 (NIV): "Search me, God, and know my heart; test me and know my anxious thoughts."
Wednesday.focus: Inspecting your own roots with God.
Wednesday.action: Take a few quiet minutes to pray this verse. Ask God to show you anything affecting your roots, such as bitterness, pride, or unhealthy influences. Write down what comes to mind and bring it to Him honestly.
Wednesday.prayer: Lord, search my heart and show me what I cannot see. Give me courage to listen to Your loving conviction and to respond. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: Hebrews 12:6 (NIV): "Because the Lord disciplines the one he loves, and he chastens everyone he accepts as his child."
Thursday.action: Think of one area where you feel something has been removed or changed. Write a short prayer entrusting it to God, and thank Him for one way He has helped you grow through a hard season.
Thursday.prayer: Father, thank You for loving me too much to leave me unchanged. Help me trust Your pruning and look for new growth. Amen.

Friday.scripture: John 7:38 (NIV): "Whoever believes in me, as Scripture has said, rivers of living water will flow from within them."
Friday.focus: Pouring out, not just taking in.
Friday.action: Do one simple act of service or encouragement today. Send an uplifting message, offer help to a neighbor, or look for a way to serve at church this month.
Friday.prayer: Jesus, let Your living water flow through me to others. Make me a contributor and not just a consumer. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: Isaiah 55:9 (NIV): "As the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways and my thoughts than your thoughts."
Saturday.focus: Trusting God's bigger picture and preparing to stay planted.
Saturday.action: Review your week and write down one lesson from each day. Then plan one concrete step to stay planted, such as attending church together, joining a group, or signing up to serve.
Saturday.prayer: Lord, thank You that Your ways are higher than mine. Keep me rooted in Your Word, Your people, and Your church, and help me bear fruit that lasts. Amen.

title: Why You’re Not Growing Spiritually | Planted to Produce
